game_concept: A survival strategy set in Mt. Pyre – Fire Shrine, an ancient fire shrine: the ash ranger must handle cinder bats while practicing data types & operators. Core idea – Arithmetic Cannon: Choose +, -, *, / or // to build a damage formula that exactly matches a shield number on cinder bats.
theme: Mt. Pyre – Fire Shrine: an ancient fire shrine
core_gameplay_loop: In Fire Shrine, repeat each round: Choose +, -, *, / or // to build a damage formula that exactly matches a shield number on cinder bats. Each round, cinder bats strike the obsidian gate, so respond before the next strike lands. Then check the damage value and advance.
secondary_mechanics: Hint tokens that reveal one line of code
player_objective: Protect the obsidian gate from cinder bats in Fire Shrine: keep the damage meter above zero by applying the concept correctly until the 46-second timer ends.
controls: Code-editor: type or edit short lines in the code panel and press Run; click to select targets.
lose_condition: damage drops to 0, or lives reach 0, before the 46-second timer ends.
learning_alignment: Week 2 – Data Types & Operators | Level 2 (intro tier): Arithmetic Cannon
assets_style: pixel-art volcano: purple-black rock, glowing lava rivers, orange ember light, drifting ash; flat Kenney-style sprites; low war drums, rumbling bass and crackling fire effects

tutorial: Step 1: Look at the code panel. It shows how damage changes.
Step 2: Use the controls to apply the code idea against cinder bats in Fire Shrine.
Step 3: Win by meeting the goal: Timer reaches 46 seconds while damage > 0.
